about.title: About Me
about.description: Senior .NET engineer moving into applied AI: I integrate LLM systems into enterprise software, and I measure them before I claim anything about them.
paragraphs: Ten years of production .NET across judicial and government systems — APIs, microservices, SSIS/ETL pipelines, SQL Server and PostgreSQL at scale, Kafka and Debezium for change data capture, Docker and Kubernetes to ship it. That is the half of AI engineering that is just engineering, and it is the half most demos skip.

The AI work is built the same way. My flagship is an Arabic legal RAG system where the question set, the reference checker and the scoreboard were written before the retriever existed. Four retrieval configurations are compared under bootstrap confidence intervals; generation is scored by a program that audits every citation against the articles the retriever actually returned, with no judge model in the loop.

It reports a negative result on purpose: adding a cross-encoder reranker cost 64x the latency and did not beat dense retrieval on this eval set. Knowing that — and knowing the eval set is too small to resolve the difference — is worth more than a demo that answers one question well.

items.title: Arabic Legal RAG — measured retrieval and citation-forced generation
items.problem: Arabic legal text breaks a RAG pipeline silently. The PDF stores text in visual order, so every word extracts reversed; Arabic-Indic digits sit inside the Arabic Unicode block, so a naive reversal turns article 25 into article 52 — a real article, wrong number, no error; and the normalisation that genuinely helps retrieval inflates the score if it is reused at evaluation time.
items.description: Article-level corpus, a hand-written question set with machine-verified article references, and four retrieval configurations compared under bootstrap confidence intervals. Generation is citation-forced and audited by a program rather than a judge model: every citation is resolved against the corpus and against the exact articles the retriever returned.

metrics.label: Reranker latency cost, for no measurable gain

items.limitation: 15 scored questions. Only dense > BM25 survives the confidence intervals — dense, hybrid and hybrid+rerank overlap, so this eval set cannot order them. The corpus also failed its fidelity check against the official gazette, so every number is performance on this corpus, not a statement about the law.

evidence.command: python evals/ablation_result.py  |  python evals/retrieval_latency.py --reps 3 --warmup 3  |  python tasks.py answer-eval --model ollama:gemma3:4b
evidence.environment: Retrieval on CPU, 12 cores / 15.9 GB. Generation on gemma3:4b via Ollama, Q4_K_M, greedy, temperature 0.
evidence.dataset: 56 articles (Egypt Law 151/2020). 20 questions — 15 scored, 5 abstention, dev split, k=5.
evidence.note: Each harness refuses to describe a dirty worktree: it runs git status itself and stamps worktree_clean into its own output, so a result produced from an edited tree says so.

items.title: Intent Router — fine-tuned encoder against a prompted LLM
items.problem: Train a small classifier, or just prompt an LLM? The question usually gets answered by instinct. Here it was answered by running both over the same bilingual (Arabic/English) labelled set and measuring accuracy, latency and throughput.
items.description: A fine-tuned multilingual DistilBERT against a self-hosted LLM with schema-constrained JSON output, behind a .NET 8 Minimal API that validates and forwards to the Python service through a typed HttpClient.

metrics.label: LLM accuracy, with no training at all

items.limitation: 32 held-out examples and no confidence intervals — one example is 3.1 points, so the accuracy gap is a direction, not a margin. The cost column in the repo is modelled from an assumed hourly host rate, never billed, and is labelled as such.

evidence.environment: Encoder on CPU; qwen2.5:7b-instruct through Ollama.
evidence.note: The harness records no device metadata, so the README states that the split between CPU and GPU is not in the record rather than guessing at it.
